text.content:
The Basics

  • The System: Outside the Wire (OTW) – 2d10 Operations System. This is a standalone Quickstart; all necessary lite mechanics, combat rules, and character sheets are located in this packet.

  • Need to play: 2 D10 dice (A third is best for a sunlight dial); pen and paper; color print maps; for skirmish play, mini model list on page 51); and solo play print the flowsheet and control sheet.

  • The Setting: This scenario takes place within a modern asymmetric conflict. Players are deployed on a counterinsurgency mission in a semi-rural district characterized by mud-brick homes, scattered farmland, and minimal civilian infrastructure, lacking reliable power, communications networks, and formal government services. All player actions unfold under the persistent observation of the local civilian population, where perception and conduct carry operational consequences.

  • Lethality: Grounded, lethal, and vulnerable. Players portray a standard military squad (1st Squad). They are heavily armed but operate under strict constraints. Combat is fast and deadly.

  • Main Focus & Theme: Tension, pressure, and consequence. This is not a combat-optimization puzzle or a "clear the map" game. The core theme is decision-making under extreme ambiguity, where restraint is an active skill and escalation creates future problems.

  • How to Run This: Procedural and pressure-driven. Do not railroad the players into outcomes, but strictly enforce time constraints and consequences. For solo play, enemies act on procedural logic.

  • Special Rules: * Campaign Tracks (Trust, Insurgent Activity, Command): Tracked dynamically throughout the session (Pages 6-7).

    • Civilian Friction Dilemmas: High-stakes, timed moral choices (Pages 31).

    • The Sunlight Clock: For solo play pacing and AI tracking (Page 15).

What is happening in the region? The players are assisting local forces fight against an insurgent force. Recently, coalition forces eliminated a local insurgent mortar team.

What is happening today? A VIP (a senior Colonel) is scheduled to transit through the Area of Operations under the escort of Company A. Standard military doctrine dictates that the Main Supply Route (MSR) must be cleared of mines and ambush indicators before the VIP moves.

What is happening right now? It is 0300 (pre-dawn). The players (1st Squad) are deploying from Fort Qalat to secure the MSR, insert a sniper overwatch team at Checkpoint 1, and link up with Company A at Checkpoint 2 to bring the Colonel home.

(🩻SPOILER WARNING FOR PLAYERS)

The Plot (The Next 3-4 Hours of Gameplay): The mission is a psychological trap. The insurgents know the VIP is moving and understand coalition escort doctrine perfectly. As the players sweep the road to Checkpoint 2, a "Civilian Friction" dilemmas in their path (e.g., a wounded child or a blocked road) that delay them, stress their timeline, and force them into hasty decisions.

Once the players turn back around, the trap springs. The insurgents believe that the VIP is with the players, and have established a hastily laid IED strike. The insurgents are trying to rush the players to a prepared killbox (near the player’s own sniper overwatch position).

Where the GM Should Pay Attention:

  • The Clock: Time is your primary weapon. Use the 60-second and 90-second real-world decision timers during the Civilian Dilemma (Phase 3) and the Ambush (Phase 6). If players hesitate, penalize their "Command" track.

  • Do Not Punish Empathy with Death: If the players stop to help civilians, do not shoot them for it. Punish their timeline and predictability. Helping civilians builds Trust but allows the insurgents time to set a deadlier trap.

  • The "Quiet Success": Remind your players that if they manage to navigate the route, avoid civilian casualties, de-escalate, and extract the VIP without turning the MSR into a warzone, they have achieved the ultimate victory. If nothing dramatic happens, they did their job.

Every solo session follows the same loop:

  1. Brief the Mission
    What are you trying to accomplish, and under what constraints?

  2. Move Through the Map
    Advance cautiously. Movement creates exposure.

  3. Resolve Contact
    Use Enemy AI and combat rules when opposition appears.

  4. Draw Events When Friction Occurs
    Hesitation, noise, or escalation invites complications.

  5. Adjust Campaign Tracks
    Your actions change Trust, Insurgent Activity, and Command Pressure.

  6. Extract, De-escalate, or Escalate
    You may always withdraw. Staying longer is a choice.

As each event is resolved, repeat this loop as the players issue new goals (missions) and move between locations on the map.

The Most Important Rule

If you are unsure what happens next, ask the Oracle.

Ask when unsure:

  • Is the area under observation?
  • Do insurgents escalate or observe?
  • Are civilians present?
  • Does Command pressure increase? Answer using:
    • Insurgent Track
    • Local Trust Track
    • Command Track

It answers Yes / No questions with consequences.

pages.name: Solo - Who Am I Playing Right Now

text.content:
A Role Focus Declaration per phase:

  • Phase 1–3: Patrol Lead
  • Phase 4: Sniper Lead
  • Phase 5-6: Patrol Lead (Snipers as Asset)

A mission that ends:

  • without contact
  • without civilian harm
  • without compromise

…is often the best possible outcome.

Withdrawal is not retreat. Withdrawal is decision-making under constraint.

The core element of Outside the Wire is a sandbox design where the ecosystem follows from session to session.

Gamemaster's Role

As the Game Master, you are not guiding players down a pre-written path to a final boss fight. Instead, you manage a living ecosystem of pressure, politics, and violence.

Tracks

The campaign dynamics revolve around three main tracks that players must navigate: Local Trust, Insurgent Activity, and Command Confidence. Each decision impacts these tracks, shaping the unfolding narrative. Each track goes from 0-10.

  • Local Trust – the willingness of the population to cooperate, tolerate presence, or remain neutral. Low Trust means villagers may mislead or refuse assistance to patrols, while high Trust could lead to providing crucial intel or safe passage.

  • Insurgent Activity – the ability of armed groups to operate, recruit, and adapt.High Insurgent Activity can lead to frequent ambushes or increased IED threats, while low might result in fewer attacks and easier patrol routes.

  • Command Confidence – the degree to which higher headquarters tolerates risk, ambiguity, and restraint. Low Command Confidence might restrict resources and support, such as airstrikes or artillery, whereas high confidence ensures ample support and authority to carry out missions effectively.

Quick Reference Summary (With DRM)

LOCAL TRUST
(0-10)

0-3: HOSTILE
(-5 Social, shelters enemy)

4-6: SUSPICIOUS
(-2 Social, misleads)

7-8: NEUTRAL
(cautious cooperation)

9-10: FRIENDLY
(+2 Social, early warning)

INSURGENT ACTIVITY
(0-10)

0-3: DEGRADED
(tactics +2, scattered)

4-6: DEGRADED
(hit-and-run only)

7-8: ACTIVE
(-2 tactics)

9-10: CONTROLS AO
(-5 tactics, adaptation)

COMMAND CONFIDENCE
(0-10)

0-3: RIP IMMINENT
(no assets)

4-6: LOW
(basic only, no air/artillery)

7-8: GOOD
(mortars, standard support)

9-10: PRIORITY
(armor/air unlocked)

To clarify consequence resolution: once a decision is made, consequences will be tracked through narrative cues, shifts in player morale, or tactical advantages or setbacks.

For instance, if a player prioritizes civilian aid over mission objectives, Trust might increase (+1 on the Trust scale), while Command might suffer a -1 shift due to unmet mission objectives, creating a tangible trade-off. The GM will inform players of these developments through descriptive narration and direct updates to the tracking system. Implement a simple tracking system, such as tokens or tally marks, to visually track consequences, such as Trust or Command approval. As each phase progresses, allow players to see markers move, increasing their investment in the unfolding narrative and long-term fallout.

SOLO DECISION PRIORITY RULE

When multiple reasonable options exist and no rule dictates priority: Choose the option that preserves ambiguity and limits escalation.

ACT RESOLUTION LOOP (Use Every Act)

1. Resolve the Act’s core roll

2. Roll Insurgent Reaction (if applicable)

3. Adjust Campaign Tracks

4. Decide: Continue or Withdraw

Withdrawal is always allowed.

CORE ORACLES

(Replace GM Fiat)

Ask when unsure:

  • Is the area under observation?

  • Do insurgents escalate or observe?

  • Are civilians present?

  • Does Command pressure increase?

Answer using:

  • Insurgent Table

  • Local Trust Table

  • Command Table

SOLO COMPRESSION RULE

If you feel overloaded by simultaneous threats, NPCs, or decisions, you may collapse an entire phase into a single roll.

  • Roll Tactics or Instinct

  • On success: favorable outcome, limited escalation

  • On partial: mixed outcome, +1 Friction

  • On failure: enemy advantage or narrative complication

Apply Campaign Track changes and move on.

The sunlight clock serves to increase pressure on player actions. The Insurgent Activity AI card directly relates to each number on the sunlight die. While GMs have complete ability to act as the insurgents, the Insurgent Activity card provides solo play with a measured opponent.

THE INSURGENT ACTIVITY AI CARD

Do not roll the Oracle to see what the enemy does. Use this behavior logic.

STATE: PASSIVE (Sunlight 1-3)

• If you are LOUD (Shooting/Vehicle): They place a “Spotter” token on your flank. +1 Insurgent Activity.

• If you are QUIET: They remain hidden. You find only “Signs of passage” (footprints, casings).

STATE: ALERT (Sunlight 4-8 OR After First Contact)

• If you HOLD POSITION: They Flank. (Spawn 1d10 Militia on your side/rear)

• If you ADVANCE: They Ambush. Attack from cover. They possess Initiative.

• If you WITHDRAW: They Harass. (Sniper fire from distance, but they do not pursue)

STATE: AGGRESSIVE (Sunlight 9-10)

• ALL ACTIONS: They launch a complex attack (Mortars + Small Arms). They want to pin you in the dark.

Loud actions are Player-initiated Gunfire or Explosions inside the patrol zone. Insertion vehicles do not count unless brought into the village

THE SUNLIGHT CLOCK

You do not have a GM to tell you when the sun goes down.

Place a d10 on the table set to 1. This is the Sunlight Die.

1-3: SUNRISE Visibility -1, Cooler

4-6: LATE MORNING Full Visibility, foot traffic

7-8: NOON Full visibility, Hot, quiet

9-10: AFTERNON Mission Failure if not with the VIP

ADVANCE THE SUNLIGHT DIE BY +1 WHEN:

1. You move between major terrain features (e.g., crossing the wadi to the village)

2. You spend time interacting with locals

3. You engage in combat for more than 3 rounds

pages.name: Solo Procedure: Advancing The Sunlight Clock

text.content:
Purpose:

The Sunlight Clock advances based on time spent, player tempo, and friction, not strict real-time tracking. A way for the battlefield to evolve without strict timekeeping. While created for solo play, GM's use allows the scenario to gain a sense of urgency.

Starting State:

Sunlight Clock begins at Morning (Full Light)

Route: FOB → CP1 → CP2 → Return | VIP: Colonel | Threat: Herding Ambush

ACT I — THE ROUTE

0300–0600

Preparation · Insertion · Tension

▸ ENTRY CONDITIONS

Depart FOB pre-dawn. Four armored vehicles. Sniper team attached.

Mission: Clear MSR, insert snipers at CP1, link with Company A at CP2.

1 PRE-MISSION PREP

Where players sit determines exposure, casualties, and chaos.

☐ Assign vehicles and seating (matters later)

☐ Choose gunner positions

☐ Decide sniper distribution

☐ Conduct PCCs/PCIs

2 MOVEMENT TO CP1

The quiet is not peace. It's a held breath before the exhale.

☐ Mount up in darkness

☐ Blacked-out headlights, radio checks

☐ Fields and ditches slide past

☐ Nothing happens—this is deliberate

3 SNIPER INSERT (CP1)

Ask: "What do the snipers do if you don't come back?"

☐ Short halt, troops dismount casually

☐ Snipers fade into terrain

☐ Vehicles remount and depart

☐ Snipers go dark—eyes only unless it goes bad

4 CONTINUE TO CP2

Something important has been left behind. The road pulls you forward.

☐ Roll out from CP1

☐ Light is stronger now

☐ Ten minutes down the MSR... ☐ Civilian Friction triggers

➤ EXIT ACT I: Snipers inserted. Patrol en route. Then the dilemma appears.

ACT II — THE DILEMMA

0600–0900

Decision · Delay · Manipulation

▸ ENTRY CONDITIONS

Civilian friction encountered. 60-second timer starts. Every delay costs.

⬅ FRICTION LOOP — Decide or Lose Command

A ROLL CIVILIAN DILEMMA (1D10)

1-2: Bleeding passenger

3-4: Blocked road

5-6: Injured child

7-8: Civilian mob

9-10: Broken CASEVAC vehicle

A child lies wounded. A man flees. No immediate threats detected.

B 60-SECOND DECISION

☐ Start real-world timer

☐ One primary action only

☐ One secondary task allowed

☐ No "perfect coverage" solutions

If no decision when timer ends → –1 Command AND –1 Trust immediately.

C RESOLVE & APPLY

☐ Aid → Trust +1, Timeline breaks

☐ Ignore → Trust –1, Command +0

☐ Half-measures → Command –1

☐ One roll only: First Aid, Instinct, or Tactics

Whatever you do will be seen. The harm comes later.

D SNIPER REPORT

☐ Radio crackles—urgent edge

☐ Insurgents setting up near CP1

☐ PKMs, IEDs, motorcycles observed

☐ Roll Tactical (Easy –5) for hide site

"This looks deliberate. Recommend reassessment."

➤ EXIT ACT II: Company A orders: "Turn around, return to CP1."

ACT III — THE TRAP

0900–1200

Ambush · Leadership · Consequence

▸ ENTRY CONDITIONS

Returning to CP1. Civilians fleeing MSR. Motorcycle scouts tracking you.

1 IED AMBUSH CHECK

The ruts aren't random. Daisy-chained. Seconds from where they want you.

☐ Roll Tactics (Hard +5) to spot daisy-chain

☐ Success → See the trap before it springs

☐ Failure → Hasty IED detonates

1D10: 1-3 Lead hit | 4-6 Lead+2nd | 7-9 Three | 10 All

2 90-SECOND DECISION

No hybrids. No sequencing. Choose one order to patrol, one to snipers.

☐ ASSAULT THROUGH → Tactics roll

☐ BREAK CONTACT → Tactics roll

☐ ANCHOR & HOLD → Wait for Company A

☐ Snipers: ENGAGE or STAY HIDDEN?

3 RESOLVE & EXTRACT

The insurgents believed the Colonel was already with you. You were herded.

☐ Success → Order works

☐ Failure → Partial success + arrival Company A

☐ If 3+ vehicles killed → Company A arrives

☐ "We've got it from here." Patrol agency ends.

OUTCOMES

✔ VIP SAFE: Colonel reaches FOB. Route cleared. Snipers recovered.

✖ EXTRACTED: VIP survives. Company A takes control. Casualties. Scrutiny.

✖ COLLAPSE: Mission fails. Casualties mount. Trust collapses. Command –2.

FINAL SOLO REMINDER: If nothing dramatic happens, the patrol probably did its job. Escalation solves today and ruins tomorrow. Ask: "Was this worth it?"
